title: Performance
purpose: Will this change make the product slower for a real tenant, on a real phone, at real data sizes? Thresholds (LCP, INP, bundle size, query time) belong to PAP-87 and PAP-242; this rubric names the patterns a reviewer can see in a diff before any budget runs, so a finding here without a measured threshold is S2 unless it is unbounded.
scope: Queries, loops, renders, bundles, payloads and jobs in the diff; test suite duration.
notCovered: Budget numbers and their enforcement (PAP-87 web budgets, PAP-242 API and database budgets).

S0: A background job loads every row of a tenant table into memory with no limit: the 8 GB host falls over (broken build in production terms).
S1: A list endpoint returns unbounded results because the new filter bypasses the `limit` clamp.
A render loop re-fetches on every keystroke with no debounce and no abort.
S2: N+1 query in a loop over 20 rows.
A 300 KB dependency added for one formatting helper.

items.title: Bundle growth
items.test: Does the diff add a dependency, a large asset or a non-lazy import to a route that noticeably grows the initial bundle, or import a whole library for one function?
items.verify: `size-limit` or the build's chunk report; check for deep imports and lazy routes; cite the added bytes when measured.

items.title: N+1 and unbounded queries
items.test: Can I find a query inside a loop, a join-less fetch per row, a query without `limit`, or a count over an unindexed predicate?
items.verify: Read every `await db.` inside `for`, `map` or `Promise.all`; check `limit <= 100` (S1 when unbounded on a user-facing list); check the index exists for new `where` columns.
items.falsePositives: Loops bounded by a small enum with a comment saying so.

items.title: Render churn
items.test: Can I type or hover and cause a whole list or table to re-render, an effect to fire every render (missing deps), or a new object identity to break memoisation?
items.verify: React profiler on the changed page; look for inline object props to memoised children, effects without deps, and state lifted higher than needed.
items.falsePositives: Small trees where the churn is measured under 16 ms.

items.title: Main-thread blocking
items.test: Can I supply a large but plausible input (10 000 rows, a 5 MB document) and freeze the UI for over 100 ms in synchronous parsing, sorting, hashing or layout?
items.verify: Run the operation with the large fixture under CPU throttle (Gate 4); long tasks in the trace; work moved to a worker or chunked.
items.falsePositives: One-off imports with a progress indicator.

items.title: Unbounded payloads and memory
items.test: Can I make a request, event or job carry or hold an unbounded array, an entire file in memory, or a stream buffered to completion?
items.verify: Body size limits on routes, streaming for files, `limit` on every collection payload, caps in the event envelope; cite the missing bound.
items.falsePositives: Internal payloads bounded by the producer's own limit, with a link to it.

items.title: Caching and repeated work
items.test: Can I find the same expensive computation, fetch or permission check repeated per render, per row or per request with no memo, cache or batching where the result is stable?
items.verify: Look for repeated `can()` calls per row, repeated `JSON.parse` of the same string, repeated formatter construction (`new Intl.*` in a loop).
items.falsePositives: Work that is trivially cheap (under a microsecond) or must be fresh.

items.title: Slow tests and CI time
items.test: Does the diff add tests that sleep, hit the network, start real servers per test, or add more than 30 s to the suite without a reason?
items.verify: Compare Gate 1 duration before and after; grep for `setTimeout` in tests, unmocked fetch, per-test container start.

items.title: Budgets when measured
items.test: Does a Gate 1 performance artefact (`perf.json`, PAP-87 or PAP-242) show a budget regression attributable to this diff?
items.verify: Read `reports/perf.json` when present and cite the metric, the budget and the delta; until PAP-87 lands record `n/a`.
items.falsePositives: Regressions inside the run-to-run noise band the budget declares.
